title: The Clock on the Table
subtitle: 习惯自律 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 习惯自律（生活与学习·良好习惯与自律）
meta: 主题语境：习惯自律（生活与学习·良好习惯与自律）　|　核心词汇：sense　|　正文 372 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sense 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: My grandfather got up at five every morning for forty years. He said the hour itself gave him a ① sense of order: while the house was still quiet, he could finish one task before anybody asked him for anything. Even at eighty his five ② senses were sharp — he could smell rain before it came and hear my step on the stairs.

When I entered senior high I decided to try it for one term. The first week my body ③ sensed nothing unusual; I simply lost an hour of sleep. I kept a notebook and wrote down one line each evening. After three weeks I tried to ④ make sense of those lines slowly, the way you read a difficult page twice, and began to see where my afternoons had gone.

The method itself was simple. It did not ⑤ make sense to anybody else at first. My plan was to review vocabulary for twenty minutes before breakfast, and to repeat the same twenty minutes every day. Discipline, I came to see, is not built by one big decision. My mother said it was only ⑥ common sense, and gave me a small clock as a reward.

One evening I tried to explain the plan to my younger brother, who is nine. 'Why get up when nobody makes you?' he asked. I spent a week thinking about his question. At first I had no answer, and he noticed that. Then he asked whether he could use my clock, and I felt a strong ⑦ sense of pride — stronger than any prize. ⑧ In a sense he was right, and ⑨ there is no sense in forcing a nine-year-old into a plan he does not believe in. I lent him the clock and said nothing.

The habit itself has stayed with me for three years. My marks have risen slowly, steadily, without drama, and my afternoons no longer disappear. We teach ourselves, in the end, only what we are ready to learn. Last month my brother asked for a notebook of his own. ⑩ In a sense that is the real reward: one small act, repeated until the body senses it as its own, quietly becomes who you are. Looking back now, the whole thing makes sense to me.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 感官；感觉官能（five senses）
B. n. ……感；意识（a sense of order/pride）
C. n. 判断力；常识（common sense）
D. v. 感觉到；意识到
E. 固定搭配：make sense 讲得通；有意义
F. 固定搭配：make sense of 弄懂；理解
G. 固定搭配：in a sense 在某种意义上
H. 固定搭配：there is no sense in doing 做某事没有意义

items.q: gave him a sense of order
I tried to make sense of those lines
It did not make sense to anybody else
In a sense he was right
there is no sense in forcing a nine-year-old
In a sense that is the real reward

answers.why: a sense of＋抽象名词，表示“……感”，这里指清晨带给他的“秩序感”。
five senses 指五种感官，后文 smell、hear 正是对感官的具体说明。
主语是 my body，后接宾语从句，sense 作动词用，意为“感觉到”，这里说身体起初没什么特别感觉。
make sense of＋宾语，意为“看懂、弄懂”那些记录，与下文 began to see 呼应。
make sense（不带宾语）意为“讲得通、说得通”，这里说这方法起初别人看不懂。
common sense 是固定说法，意为“常识”，母亲觉得早起学习只是常识罢了。
a strong sense of pride＝“强烈的自豪感”，与第 1 题同属“……感”，注意 pride 换成 success、direction 也同义。
in a sense 位于句首，意为“在某种意义上”，表示作者部分承认弟弟说得对。
there is no sense in doing sth 意为“做某事没有意义”，后接 forcing，说明不该强迫。
同样是 in a sense，意为“在某种意义上”，引出作者认为真正的收获是什么。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 清晨的时光给他一种秩序感。（a sense of）
三周后，我试图弄懂笔记本上那些句子。（make sense of）
起初这个方法对每个同学来说都说不通。（make sense）
母亲说这不过是常识。（common sense）
在某种意义上，我弟弟是对的。（in a sense）
把一个九岁的孩子推进他不相信的计划里毫无意义。（there is no sense in）
answers: The early morning gave him a sense of order.
Three weeks later I tried to make sense of the lines in my notebook.
At first the method did not make sense to any of my classmates.
My mother said it was only common sense.
In a sense my younger brother was right.
There is no sense in pushing a nine-year-old into a plan he does not believe in.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 sense 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: The habit itself gives me a sense of order that no timetable has ever given me.
I repeat the same twenty minutes every morning until my body senses it as its own.
It did not make sense to my classmates at first, and honestly it hardly made sense to me either.
In a sense, self-discipline is nothing but common sense practised every single day.
There is no sense in copying somebody else's plan if you do not believe in it yourself.
My marks have risen steadily, and though five senses cannot measure a habit, every morning I can feel it working.
